extracted.intended_audience: art historians, architects, painters, and students of Renaissance art
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted standards and qualities used in Vasari's Lives to praise or criticize Renaissance painters and architects — covering technical methods, aesthetic qualities, structural practice, and moral/religious suitability. Useful for judging workmanship, design, and professional conduct in Renaissance-era art and architecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence and devotion to art
rubrics_metrics.description: Works 'executed with such diligence that it brought him praise and honour' and created 'without grudging time or labour'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari praises artists who spend long, patient labour on their works, refuse to hurry completion, and are willing to endure personal discomfort for the pursuit of art (e.g., eating poorly, working for pleasure rather than comfort). Such diligence is presented as producing 'truly beautiful' results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth to nature and investigation of Nature's secrets
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'certain subtlety in the investigation of some of the deepest and most subtle secrets of Nature' and 'most vivid truth to nature' in depiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists should study and render natural variety and subtle natural phenomena; a deep, curious investigation of nature yields lifelike, convincing figures and scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety, characterization, and graceful composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The diversity seen in Piero's bacchanalian scenes — 'diversity of the bay horses and garments, and the variety of the goatlike features, and all with great grace'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful compositions show varied, well-characterized figures and details while maintaining overall grace; variety should not sacrifice harmony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and distinctive spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition of 'a spirit very different and far distant from that of other painters' and 'very varied and original in his discourse'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality in conception, manner, and discourse is lauded; a unique artistic voice or unusual approach can mark greatness, even if eccentric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery of both theory and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: An architect (Bramante) 'had the mastery not of theory only, but of supreme skill and practice.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great practitioners combine learned theoretical knowledge (proportion, Orders) with consummate practical skill in execution and construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion, invention, and thorough knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Works characterized by 'greater invention and proportion, or with a more thorough knowledge' were held to be superior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designs should show inventive solutions while adhering to sound proportions and well-grounded knowledge of classical precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to architectural detail and the Orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Careful contrivance of 'the outlines of the cornices, the shafts of the columns, the graceful capitals, the bases, the consoles and corners, the vaults, the staircases, the projections, and every detail of every Order of architecture.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excellent architecture attends to every component and ornament of the Orders; success is measured by the harmony and correctness of these elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study and measurement of antiquities inform design
rubrics_metrics.description: Bramante 'measured all the buildings in that city and in the Campagna' and used these measurements in his work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful measurement and study of ancient examples provide essential knowledge and inspiration; designers should record and apply empirical data from antiquities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of models and preparatory designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Bramante and others 'made a model for the whole' and 'made many designs and models for palaces and temples'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparation of accurate models and drawings is essential for conceiving complex projects and communicating invention to patrons and builders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy and independence to permit scholarly work
rubrics_metrics.description: Bramante 'brought some money... and this he spent with the greatest economy, since he wished to be able to live independently, and at the same time... to take measurements... at his ease.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining financial independence or economy can enable extended study and careful planning; personal management affects the capacity to pursue high-quality work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promptness and expedition in execution (with caution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many works were 'executed by him with extraordinary speed' and 'with supreme expedition and art.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speed and decisiveness in construction are virtues when combined with sound technique, but haste without oversight can produce defects; balance promptness with proper supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper supervision and care of foundations and construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Because foundations were made 'without seeing anything more of the work' (sand and clay brought by night), 'all his buildings have cracked' — attributing cracking to inadvertence in foundation work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct oversight of foundations and early construction stages is critical; negligent or secretive handling of foundational work can cause long-term structural failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural prudence: avoid weakening walls with internal passages
rubrics_metrics.description: Ventura 'made within the thickness of the wall... a passage that runs right round, whereby he contrived to weaken the walls so much' that vaulting was dangerous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design choices that reduce wall strength (e.g., continuous internal passages) must be evaluated against loads; ensure adequate buttressing, thickness, or reinforcement before vaulting heavy tribunes or domes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of buttresses, reinforcement, and iron keys for stability
rubrics_metrics.description: Vasari reinforced Ventura's structure by 'making buttresses' and 'binding the corners... with stout keys of iron, double at the angles', enabling the vault to be raised safely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where original construction weakened a building, add buttresses, ties, and metal reinforcement to safely redistribute loads and allow vaulting or domes to be built.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical innovation in construction and surface treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Bramante 'invented the method of casting vaults in wooden moulds' and knew 'the secret of stucco'; these were ancient techniques restored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study and revive proven technical methods (e.g., moulded vaults, stucco ornamentation) or invent practical methods to achieve ornamental or structural effects; technical mastery counts as a mark of genius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional invention and mobility in design
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: 'a spiral staircase upon mounting columns, in such a way that one can ascend it on horseback', with Orders passing from Doric to Ionic to Corinthian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ingenious, functional design that solves programmatic needs while integrating aesthetic transitions is highly prized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohesion of ornament and immutability of successful designs
rubrics_metrics.description: The interior cornice is 'so graceful, that no other man's hand could take away or alter anything from its design without spoiling it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great designs achieve a unity where later alterations tend to degrade the whole; strive for cohesive ornament-structure relationships that resist arbitrary modification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressive clarity and moral content in religious painting
rubrics_metrics.description: In Baccio's unfinished Judgment fresco 'one sees the despair, grief, and shame of everlasting death, even as one perceives contentment and gladness in those that are being saved.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious works should clearly convey moral and emotional states appropriate to their subjects; expressive clarity and the ability to move the viewer are key measures of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soft colouring and beautiful drapery
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures described as 'soft in colouring and most beautifully draped.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delicate handling of colour and skilful depiction of drapery enhance the dignity and lifelikeness of figures; mastery of colour modulation and fabric rendering is a virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter suitability and avoidance of lascivious images in sacred contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Fra Girolamo Savonarola 'crying out every day... that lascivious pictures, music, and amorous books often lead the mind to evil', and that it 'was not right to keep in houses where there were young girls painted figures of naked men and women.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious and devotional contexts demand modest, edifying subject matter; painters working for religious patrons must consider moral suitability and the likely spiritual effect of imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional reputation built through notable commissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Completion of important chapels, cloisters, palaces, and public works brought fame and commissions; 'this work gave him a very great name.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality public and ecclesiastical commissions establish reputation; successful execution of large, visible projects demonstrates capability and attracts further patrons.
